note: Room 3, the Bountiful Nugget. Derived by measurement from the gridded plate the way Room 2's was, for Tyler to confirm. The camera looks ALONG the room: the street wall with the batwing doors and window is on the left, the bar runs away down the right, and the back wall closes it about two-thirds up. TWO RECTS ARE PROVISIONAL: the patrons and Deke Vessel are sprites that do not exist yet, so their rects are placeholders and must be re-derived from where the figures actually stand. THE PATRONS RECT IS NO LONGER PROVISIONAL: derived from the bounding box of the five placed groups, which is the rule -- a rect for people follows the people.

scaling.note:
FITTED TO THE CARD PLAYERS, the group Tyler says could belong in this game. They are 282px standing-equivalent with their feet at y508; Thad is now 281 there and 340 at the front.
Three fits have been tried. To the bar men: 459 at the front and he doubled walking through the doors. To the game’s other rooms: 260, and half the size of the men at the bar. To the card players: 340, which is the only anchor in this room that Tyler has said reads correctly. The bar men remain 1.22x him and are the group he says does not belong -- that is a regeneration, not a curve.

entrances.note: Through the batwing doors on the left wall, facing right into the room.
Anything else arrives by the door.

obstacles.note: The stool in front of the piano. He walks round it, not through it.

Brass, on the floor, and emptied more diligently than anything else in the building. He walks round it. Same rect as the hotspot, so the thing you click and the thing you cannot walk through are one truth.
The table, its chairs and the four men are one sprite; this is its footprint on the floor, which he walks round.

provisional.deke_vessel: ACT II, NOT ACT I. Doc 02 A3 puts the swindle in this room and the room gate flagged him for it, but doc 04 VES_A1 says the sale is "staged in the opening’s shadow: he is gone by the time the player can act". His standing appearance is VES_B1, "found again, Duel One", in Act II. So he is act-gated like the raccoon, and this rect is where he will stand when he is here.
provisional.raccoon: ACT II ONWARD, after A5. He takes up residence on the END OF THE BAR -- doc 05: "I evicted him from a hole and he has been promoted" -- so the rect is on the bar top near the front, and it is provisional until the sprite exists and can be measured, the same as Vessel.

walkableNote: The right edge follows the BAR GROUP’S OWN SILHOUETTE, read off the three shipped sprites composited together rather than estimated from the plate. That is the correct boundary because the men standing at the counter are part of the same object: floor Thad cannot walk through, whether it is oak or a drinker. Measured after the bar was refitted -- the first polygon was drawn against the OLD bar, which sat 432px further into the room.

lamps.note: Seven candles over the middle of the room. The slowest and widest of the three.
A fire in an iron box, and doc 05 says the pipe was fitted by somebody who had seen a stove. It flickers hardest and fastest.
The wall lamps behind the bar, together. Barely moving -- they are trimmed, because the barman is the only person in town who maintains anything.

handNote: Doc 16: "a hand of cards, face up, ABANDONED... somebody left a very good hand on a table and went outside." So it lies on the card table’s own top, and its rect is derived from the table group sprite rather than guessed -- it moves if the table does, which it already did once when the group shifted 35px clear of the piano.

deke_vessel.note: ACT II. Not an examine hotspot -- doc 04 VES_B1, a character with a tree, found again in this room. Provisional until the sprite exists.

raccoon.note: ACT II after A5. Doc 49 gives him TALK TO and PICK UP; doc 05 writes no examine lines because he is a mover, not scenery. On the end of the bar -- he was evicted from a hole and has been promoted.

charactersNote: Kept OUT of `hotspots` on purpose. The compiler reconciles hotspot rects against the documents that write examine lines, and correctly called these two orphans: a rect with no lines is a hotspot that says nothing when clicked. They are characters, their words live in their trees and in doc 49, and their rects follow their sprites.
idNote: Ids follow the LIVE ROOM FILE, not a slug of the doc name -- the compiler says so and it is right: a person chose `portrait` and `cards`, and I had renamed them to `faded_portrait` and `hand_of_cards` from the headings.
walkModelNote: The Nugget's floor is not a rectangle -- it narrows against the bar, from 1011px wide at the back to 1546 at the front -- so its bands are clipped to the floor’s own span at each depth. A street does not declare this: Room 2 is full width everywhere a player stands, and clipping its topmost band on the sloping boardwalk line collapsed it to 51px.
backgroundNote: Tyler's answer: replace the whole picture per frame rather than compositing anything. Safe HERE and not in general -- everything that moves in this room is always BEHIND Thad, because the floor's right edge follows the bar front and the card table sits above the floor's back edge, so he never passes in front of either. A room whose animated furniture he can walk in front of must not use this. SIX FRAMES, MIXED FROM ONE SHEET. The sheet returned four poses in which only ONE man moves per pose -- measured: 55.2, 25.8, 28.0 and 64.6 for the man who moves, and 0.0 for the men who do not, byte-identical. Re-running the prompt with "all four men move in every pose" returned the identical image, max difference 0. So the four poses are recombined instead: the only column where nobody moves in any pose is x181-187, so the sprite splits there into two halves with three and two genuine states, and six frames alternate both. Every consecutive frame changes on BOTH sides of the table.
patronsNote: THE CARD TABLE ONLY. It was derived as the bounding box of every group with a person in it, which spanned x705-1916 and y298-849 -- 667,261 pixels, forty per cent of the room, swallowing most of the floor so the player could not click to walk. A hotspot is a click target, not an inventory of everyone present: the bar’s drinkers are reachable through THE BAR, which is where a player would click for them anyway.
